This appeal under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act')
has been filed by the Insurance Company being aggrieved by the judgment dated 03.09.2018 passed by the II Additional District & Sessions Judge & Additional MACT., Hassan.

sentences.text: (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal') in MVC No.730/2017.

2. Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeal briefly stated are that on 21.01.2016 at about 9.00 p.m.,
when the claimant was proceeding on motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-18/EB-7725 near Kalasapura - Lakya NC: 2024:KHC:37268 road, at that time, another motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-13/X-528 being ridden by its rider at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, dashed to the vehicle of the claimant.
As a result of the aforesaid accident, the claimant sustained grievous injuries and was hospitalized.
3. The claimant filed a petition under Section 166 of the Act, seeking compensation.
It was pleaded that he spent significant amount towards medical expenses, conveyance charges and other related costs.

It was further pleaded that the accident occurred solely on account of rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle by its rider.
4.
Upon service of notice, the respondent No.2 appeared through counsel and filed written statement denying the averments made in the claim petition.
The respondent No.1, despite service of notice, did not appear before the Tribunal and was placed ex-parte.

sentences.text:
On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter,
recorded NC: 2024:KHC:37268 the evidence.
The claimant, in order to prove the case, examined himself as PW-1, and Dr.S.C.Kiran was examined as PW-2, and got exhibited documents namely Ex.P1 to Ex.P9.
On behalf of the respondents, one witness was examined as RW-1 and got exhibited document namely Ex.R1.
The Claims Tribunal, by the impugned judgment, inter alia
, held that the accident took place on account of rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle by its rider, as a result of which, the claimant sustained injuries.

The Tribunal further held that the claimant is entitled to a compensation of Rs.2,02,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. and directed the Insurance Company to deposit the compensation amount along with interest.

Being aggrieved,
the present appeal has been filed.

6. The learned counsel for the Insurance Company raised the following contentions:
NC: 2024:KHC:37268 (i) Firstly, the spot mahazar was drawn on 22.01.2016 in the presence of the eyewitness, but he was not examined, to prove the same.

(ii) Secondly, it was stated that the injured was first taken to Chikkamagalur Govt.
Hospital and was treated there from 21.01.2016 to 25.01.2016, but no medical records of the said hospital has been produced.

(iii) Thirdly, in the wound certificate - Ex.P2 issued by the Hassan Govt. Hospital,
dated 27.05.2016 stating that self-fall on 26.01.2016 and later, it was added with the word 'RTA' as per the affidavit dated 01.02.2016.

(iv) Fourthly, the MLC register further confirms that injured was admitted to Hassan Govt. Hospital on 26.01.2016 with H/O self fall and adding H/O hit by unknown vehicle vide affidavit dated 01.02.2016.
(v) Fifthly, the discharge summary of Hassan Govt. Hospital - Ex.P8 further discloses H/O of self fall.
Sixthly, the seizure mahazar - Ex.P3 dated 28.01.2016 was apparently created to implicate the insured vehicle.

(vii) Seventhly, as per the evidence of the doctor - PW2, the claimant was admitted H/O injury was due to self fall from bike and later it was recorded as RTA on an affidavit dated 01.02.2016 and nowhere either type of vehicle or number of vehicle is forthcoming.
(viii)
Eighthly, the finding of the Tribunal regarding negligence as well as involvement of insured motorcycle suffers from many infirmities and illegality.
Hence, he sought to allow the appeal.

sentences.text: On the other hand, the learned counsel for the claimant raised the following contentions:
(i) Firstly, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the rider of the offending vehicle.
Since the claimant was unconscious, the attender, who has come to the hospital, has wrongly given the information as self-fall.
Secondly, since the claimant suffered grievous injuries and was unconscious, he was not in a position to lodge the complaint immediately.
(iii) Thirdly, on the basis of the complaint, the police have registered FIR and after through investigation have filed the charge sheet.
Therefore, the evidence of PW1, FIR, charge sheet, spot mahazar clearly prove that the rider of the offending vehicle was negligent in causing the accident.
To disprove the same, the respondents have not examined the rider of the offending motorcycle.
The Tribunal, after considering the same, has rightly held that the rider of the offending vehicle is negligent in causing the accident.
Hence, he sought to dismiss the appeal.

8. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the judgment and award of the Tribunal and the original records.
9.

The case of the claimant is that, on 21.01.2016 at about 9.00 p.m., when the claimant was proceeding on motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-18/EB-7725 near NC: 2024:KHC:37268 Kalasapura - Lakya road, at that time, another motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-13/X-528 being ridden by its rider at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, dashed to the vehicle of the claimant.
As a result of the aforesaid accident, the claimant sustained grievous injuries.
He was immediately shifted to Government Hospital, Chikkamagalur and he has been referred to Government Hospital, Hassan.
The learned counsel for the Insurance Company contended that, in all the medical records, it is mentioned as self-fall.
The complaint has been lodged on the next day.
In the complaint, the vehicle has been mentioned as unknown.
For the first time, the vehicle name has been mentioned in the charge sheet.
To prove the same, the respondents have not examined the investigating officer.

He has also relied on the judgment of a Division Bench of this Court in the case of REGIONAL MANAGER, UNITED INDIA INSURANCE COMPANY LTD. Vs. GAYATRIDEVI AND OTHERS (MFA No.11443/2006 & connected matters, disposed of NC: 2024:KHC:37268 on 18.07.2012).

The relevant paragraph is extracted below:
" 27.

At this juncture, counsel for insurance company relied upon the judgment rendered by Division Bench of this Court in the matter of Smt.Revathi & Anr., -vs- Smt.Kiran P.Suvarna & Anr., reported in ILR 2010 KAR 5394, wherein it is held that in a situation where the involvement of vehicle was not available at the initial stage and subsequently, if vehicle involved is apprehended and against which charge sheet is filed, claimant should have examined the Investigation Officer to substantiate the same.

sentences.text: "The said claim petition had come up for consideration before the Tribunal.

The Tribunal after assessing the oral and documentary evidence and other materials available on file, has dismissed the claim petition holding that the driver of the Maruti Omni Van bearing No.KA.19/N-4461 was not involved in the accident and inspite of giving sufficient opportunity to the appellants, they have not examined the Investigating Officer."
10.
From the above, it is clear that the evidence of the investigating officer is necessary.
In view of the - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:37268 above, to give one more opportunity to the parties, the matter requires to be remitted back to the Tribunal to examine the investigating officer.

11. In the result, the following order is passed:
ORDER
(i) The appeal is allowed.
(ii) The judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is set aside.
(iii) The matter is remitted back to the Tribunal to give an opportunity to both the parties to adduce additional evidence and to produce additional documents.
(iv) The parties are directed to appear before the Tribunal on 22.10.2024, without any further notice.
(v) The Tribunal is directed to re-consider the matter afresh and pass appropriate orders, in accordance with law, without being influenced by the observations made in this order.
- 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:37268 (vi) The amount in deposit is ordered to be transferred to the Tribunal forthwith.

Sd/-
